findings.title: Rendering a small table can allocate gigabytes from an unchecked span
findings.summary: Rendering an admitted DOCX trusts `gridSpan`, `gridBefore` and `gridAfter` as allocation dimensions. A span of 1073741824 requests a 4 GiB column vector; embedded HTML `colspan` independently generates that many XML columns.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.explanation: Summed spans directly determine f32 vector length.

codeEvidence.explanation: An embedded chunk supplies a positive usize colspan.

codeEvidence.explanation: The requested logical width sets loop iterations and generated XML size.

rootCause.summary: `cell_span()` and `row_grid_skip()` parse positive document-controlled integers without a logical-column cap. `table_block()` sums those spans into `occupancy` and passes it to vector allocation. The HTML importer repeats the same missing column-bound control before generating one `gridCol` per column.

findings.remediation: Apply a supported logical-column cap to DOCX and HTML spans and row skip counts, checked-sum row occupancy, and refuse over-budget tables before allocation or XML generation.

PNG raster limits occur after layout. SECURITY.md recommends external process limits, whose presence is not established.

findings.title: Rendering one numbered paragraph can perform billions of iterations
findings.summary: A DOCX paragraph can set `ilvl` to 4000000000. The renderer searches every lower integer for a defined numbering level; supplying an oversized definition instead makes it populate billions of counters.

findings.title: Rendering repeated altChunks expands admitted content beyond package budgets
findings.summary: Rendering admits the original ZIP, then expands every HTML/MHT chunk reference without an expanded-output budget. Repeating 1000 references to one 10 MiB HTML part can create over 10 GiB of XML before DOM construction.

rootCause.summary: `with_layout()` performs package admission before `altchunk::expand()`. Expansion reloads, converts and appends each referenced chunk with no cumulative output/node/depth limit, then passes the resulting XML to the infallible DOM parser without rechecking policy.

findings.remediation: Make altChunk import fallible, budget cumulative generated bytes/nodes and import depth while building output, and apply active checked XML depth/tag policy before DOM construction.

findings.title: Sharing a scrubbed DOCX can retain authors and metadata at valid alternate part paths
findings.summary: `scrub` advertises removing authors and identifying metadata before sharing, but discovers author-bearing parts only under `word/` with `.xml` names and properties only at fixed `docProps` filenames. findings.title: An EOCD marker in a ZIP comment bypasses the archive entry budget
findings.summary: Package preflight reads the count from the last raw EOCD marker, while the ZIP reader skips invalid candidates. A fake zero-count end record in the real ZIP comment lets an archive exceeding `max_entries` be indexed and processed.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently traced actual current source, checked relevant controls and sibling operations; no application code or exploit input was executed.

codeEvidence.explanation: The count is taken from the last marker without checking its offset/record validity.

codeEvidence.explanation: The unvalidated count alone governs max_entries.

codeEvidence.label: Post-open admission check
codeEvidence.explanation: The actual count is only compared in the duplicate-loss direction.

codeEvidence.label: Independent package reader
codeEvidence.explanation: PartFs trusts the same preflight then opens/processes the consumer-selected archive.

rootCause.summary: `declared_entry_count()` trusts a signature and two count bytes without validating the record's central-directory offset. zip 9.0.5 rejects an impossible zero-count offset and resumes its backward search to the real EOCD. `admit()` only checks for fewer indexed entries than declared, while `read_package()` has no actual entry-count recheck.

findings.remediation: Make preflight select and validate the same EOCD/ZIP64 structure the consumer uses before allocating its index, and additionally enforce the actual indexed entry count. Do not trust the final signature alone.

counterEvidence: Compressed byte, per-part and total inflation budgets still apply.
Local/central content validation operates on the real selected archive; it does not compare the preflight EOCD to that archive.
Installed zip9.0.5 find_central_directory.rs149-156 rejects zero-file offsets beyond the EOCD and continues; zip_archive.rs178-235 retries candidate metadata failures.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; deployment isolation and externally imposed quotas were not supplied.

findings.title: The public Strict-format probe inflates and rescans an unbounded XML preamble
findings.summary: Calling `main_part_is_strict()` on untrusted DOCX bytes can inflate a huge compressed XML comment and repeatedly scan the entire retained prefix. The independent public probe bypasses the budgets used by ordinary conversion.

severity.rationale: High-likelihood deterministic denial of service at an untrusted document/library boundary; impact is host availability, with remote deployment and blast radius unspecified.

codeEvidence.explanation: The Strict translation module is publicly callable.

codeEvidence.explanation: A long comment body causes this scan over all accumulated text each time.

rootCause.summary: The probe opens ZIP bytes directly, reads the main entry without an inflation cap, and appends each 16 KiB chunk. A preamble beginning with a single `<!--` and no further '<' retains the entire prefix because trimming starts at its initial '<'; each `root_open()` call scans it again.

findings.remediation: Apply compressed/entry/inflation limits to the probe and scan XML preamble state incrementally without retaining or rescanning arbitrary comment bodies.
